posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
I have noticed that prepping glass plates is a souce of trouble for making your own plates. I was hoping to add some information to the wiki about it but I need some help.

This process is called snubbing?

I have used sodium hypochlorate (househole bleach) to strip gelatine. I have heard of using silane. Can anyone help me to provide directions?

> **JohnFP:** For my standard DCG I soak the plates in 5% HydroChloric Acid at least 12 hours. I then scub them with a plastic wooly used to clean no stick pans in the Acid. I then put them in running how water and scrub them again in the hot water with the plastic wooly. I then set them in a rack and before they dry completely I wipe them with a fresh clean paper towel. It is important that there is a very little moisture on the glass during this wiping. I then blow them off with air.

posts.author: glajciorz
posts.content_md:
Welcome.

I soak my plates overnight in 10% potassium hydroxide aqueous/isopropyl solution (1 part alcohol per 6 parts of water) .

I rinse them in warm tap water (rubbing with latex gloves - one side of the glass will make a sound when hydrophilic), rinse in DI/distilled water and wipe with towel paper until dry, wipe with a clean cloth (of silk for example) and blow with canned air.

2 days ago after such treatment, courtain coating (10% culinary gelatin, at 80deg.C), hardening in alum/formaldehyde (2 batches) and curing at 60deg.C I left my plates in DI water for 24 hours (to remove traces of a hardener). Today the gelatine is still fine and can be removed only by scratching with a nail.

I hope it helps.

The other way to clean plates would be soaking them in car battery acid solution with 10% potassium dichromate added. It worked with lab glass, but I haven't tried it for holographic plates. This mixture is supposed to be cancerogenic, so maybe it would be better to use KOH solution if possible.

greetings

Adam

posts.author: Cristiano_Perrucci
posts.content_md:
> **Colin Kaminski:** I have noticed that prepping glass plates is a souce of trouble for making your own plates. I was hoping to add some information to the wiki about it but I need some help.

Colin,

this is my std cleaning procedure for new plates:

1- hand wash for a few a minute with sponge and dish detergent

2- soak in 50% domestic bleach for 6-8 hrs

3- wash in hot tap water (~45C) scrubbing with a sponge for a minute

4- final wash in R.O. water for a few seconds

5- dry with a towel

6- final cleaning with Glassex (Windex in the USA?)

this procedure works fine for MBDCG

If I'm recycling old homemade plates, I start cleaning procedure from step 3 until all old emulsion has been washed out.

Cleaning plates is the most boring task of DIY holographic plates, I liked to minimize time spent for this crucial step.
